preregistered: Traced from installed alpaca-py 0.44.0 source: TradingClient.submit_order calls order_data.to_request_fields() then self.post('/orders', data), and common/rest.py._request sets opts['json']=data before self._session.request(...); requests 2.34.2's PreparedRequest.prepare_body computes body=complexjson.dumps(json, allow_nan=False) for that path. If requests.PreparedRequest().prepare_body(json=to_request_fields()) reproduces that exact call and shows qty/limit_price/notional serialized as native JSON numbers (not decimal-preserving strings) for Decimal/int/float inputs, that settles the wire-level half of gap 4 in the supports_incumbent direction (confirms the suspected float/precision loss at the literal byte level, not just at the object-field-type level). If TradingClient exposes a different private serialization method not used by submit_order, or wire bytes exactly preserve input decimal text, that would refute the incumbent's gap-4 claim. No network egress is possible (bwrap --unshare-net + audit-hook transport block) and TradingClient is constructed only with placeholder strings 'k'/'s', never a real credential.

Key findings: (1) qty is always emitted as a native JSON float regardless of whether the input was int, Decimal, or float (e.g. Decimal('1000000') -> "qty": 1000000.0, Decimal('0.5') -> "qty": 0.5); (2) trailing-zero/precision text is not preserved -- Decimal('100.10') (2 fractional digits typed) is emitted as "limit_price": 100.1 (1 digit) on the wire, confirming decimal-text loss at the literal byte level, not just at the object-field-type level the existing probe already showed; (3) notional is likewise emitted as a native float ("notional": 500.0, "notional": 500.005); (4) alpaca-py's local pydantic model performs no rejection of qty<=0 (zero_qty and negative_qty both serialized cleanly to wire bytes with no ValidationError), so any such rejection is enforced only server-side, not by the SDK; (5) no _prepare_order_data or other alternate private serialization method exists on TradingClient in 0.44.0 -- submit_order's only path is to_request_fields() -> requests' own json= handling, confirmed by source grep and by an explicit hasattr assertion in the probe that did not fail.
